transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam Brooks (Redwood SE); Ravi Menon (Redwood CSM); Rajiv Patel (Ionix - Head of IT); Sophie Carter (Ionix - Procurement); Marta Lopez (Ionix - Security); Daniel Kim (Ionix - Legal)

Summary:
Quick procurement/contracting call to review MSA and DPA open items, SLA targets, pricing commitments for Dedicated vs Hosted, onboarding timeline and PO/signature path. Ionix has SOC2 in place but wants clarifications on data residency, KMS, audit logs and the SLA credit language.

Topics:
- MSA redlines (liability, indemnity, termination)
- DPA: data processing, sub-processors, data residency, deletion/return clauses
- SLAs: latency/uptime targets for Dedicated and Hosted; credits and remediation windows
- Pricing: committed reserved capacity vs burst pricing, start-of-contract discounts, annual true-up
- Onboarding: SSO, network configuration, technical runbook and benchmarks

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we have the procurement, uh walkthrough today. I think we have the redlines in the doc, we wanted to run through them with ionix team and make sure the SLA language and DPA items are clear.
[00:22] Rajiv Patel: Yeah thanks, Maya. We got the MSA yesterday, I skimmed — there's a couple of safety items. Biggest thing for us is data residency and vendor access to logs, and, um, how you handle KMS keys.
[00:35] Liam Brooks: Sure, Rajiv — quick intro, I'm Liam on the SE side, I'll handle the technical bits. On KMS we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/HSM on Private deployments and we can crypto‑split keys for Dedicated depending on the build — sorry, that last part, um, depends on the deployment model.
[00:55] Marta Lopez: Quick question — for hosted API do you allow CMKs? We need to ensure keys are not accessible by third parties.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Hosted doesn't support customer-managed KMS out of the box today, correct, but we do have envelope encryption and we can discuss a private deployment or dedicated cluster with customer KMS. I'll let Liam confirm specifics.
[01:15] Liam Brooks: Yeah hosted uses our managed encryption with strict access controls; for CMK we recommend Dedicated or Private. If you go Dedicated we can bring the nodes into your VPC and use customer KMS for disk encryption and secrets.
[01:32] Daniel Kim: On the MSA liability cap — your standard is one year of fees — Ionix wants to cap for gross negligence excluded etc, but we'd like to see a carveout for breaches with PII. Is that something you normally negotiate?
[01:50] Maya Chen: We can be flexible on carveouts for data breach — typical negotiation is to carve out liability for willful misconduct and certain breach scenarios. We'll need legal to see their proposed language; we can take that back to our legal team.
[02:05] Sophie Carter: Process-wise, we need to know how long counter-signing usually takes — our procurement usually wants signature in 2–3 weeks after final redline. Any constraints from Redwood?
[02:20] Maya Chen: From our side once legal signs off it usually takes about a week to countersign, sometimes sooner. So two to three weeks is reasonable if redlines are not extensive.
[02:30] Rajiv Patel: SLA — Ionix expects 99.95% availability for our use-case on Dedicated, can you commit to that, and what are the credit terms?
[02:45] Liam Brooks: We have dedicated SLA tiers: Dedicated Enterprise can do 99.95% with an SLA credit of X% of monthly fees (we have the table in the SLA doc). For Hosted the SLA is lower, typically 99.9. Credits are tiered and we provide remediation windows.
[03:05] Rajiv Patel: The SLA credit definition — is it pro rata or do you have service credits that are capped to a percentage of fees? Because procurement wants sufficient remedy.
[03:18] Maya Chen: It's capped, typical market standard is 5–50% of monthly fees depending on severity. We can run specifics with legal but willing to discuss larger cap for enterprise deals.
[03:30] Marta Lopez: Also need to confirm audit logs retention for API calls — we need 12 months of immutable logs with export to our SIEM.
[03:45] Liam Brooks: We keep request logs for 90 days in hosted by default, but for Dedicated we can extend retention and export to your SIEM via S3 connectors and log forwarding, retention to 12 months is feasible.
[04:00] Daniel Kim: DPA — are your subprocessors listed and how do you handle subprocessor notifications? Ionix requires 30 days notice before material changes.
[04:12] Maya Chen: We maintain a subprocessor list in the vendor portal and provide notice; 30 days is standard ask, we can commit to that and include in DPA language.
[04:25] Sophie Carter: Pricing — we need committed capacity pricing for 3x A100‑like units or equivalent for initial pilot. Can you provide committed vs burst pricing? Also, any onboarding discount?
[04:40] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll share a pricing worksheet. Typical options: monthly reserved capacity (discounted), plus burst at on-demand rates; onboarding discounts for multi-year commitments are negotiable. I'll send the sheet after the call.
[04:55] Rajiv Patel: Benchmarks — before we sign we want a latency baseline for our prompt profile and an on‑prem run if we do private. Can you run a short perf test?
[05:08] Liam Brooks: Absolutely, we can run a benchmark. We'll need a sample prompt set and expected qps/sequence length. We can schedule a test run with our infra team; results go into the onboarding checklist.
[05:25] Sophie Carter: Procurement timeline — assuming we get SOC2 and DPA today and redlines by next week, we can get PO in by July 22. Is that realistic?
[05:35] Maya Chen: Yes that's aligned — our next steps will be to circulate the redlined MSA for legal review, share SOC2, and pricing.
[05:45] Daniel Kim: A couple legal housekeeping items — can Redwood accept mutual indemnities and carveouts for regulatory fines? Also, Termination for convenience with 60 days notice?
[06:00] Maya Chen: Mutual indemnities are sometimes accepted with reciprocal obligations; termination for convenience 60 days is a negotiable point — typically we do 30–90 days depending on seat commitments. We'll confirm with legal.
[06:15] Rajiv Patel: Any special compliance packages? We require data residency in eu-west-1 for a subset of data — can you pin region for logs and storage?
[06:28] Liam Brooks: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we can pin storage to region, for Hosted we'd need to confirm if our hosted region supports EU-only residency or handle via Private. We'll note that as a requirement.
[06:42] Ravi Menon: Onboarding — I'll own technical onboarding and liaise with Rajiv. We'll prepare a runbook and a playbook for SSO, network peering, and testing.
[06:55] Sophie Carter: Who signs the DPA — is that the same as the MSA signatory or do you require separate sign-off?
[07:05] Maya Chen: Typically the MSA signer countersigns the DPA, but we can accommodate separate signature if required.
[07:15] Rajiv Patel: Ok, sounds good. Could you also confirm encryption at rest and in transit specifics in writing? We need exact cipher suites and TLS versions.
[07:28] Liam Brooks: We'll include the crypto suite in the security pack; we support TLS 1.2+ and recommend 1.3 where possible, AES‑256 for at-rest encryption, and details about key rotation policies.
[07:42] Daniel Kim: One last question on exportability — if we terminate can we get a full export of logs and models or are outputs ephemeral?
[07:55] Maya Chen: We offer data export and a data deletion plan in the DPA. For models, outputs are customer-owned and we can deliver exports per the SOW; we'll include retention/export timeline.
[08:10] Sophie Carter: Great, to recap — Ionix will send any final redlines by next Wednesday, Redwood to send SOC2 + security pack by Friday, Redwood to send pricing worksheet and committed capacity options, and schedule a perf test.
[08:25] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll follow up with all artifacts and a proposed timeline. Thanks all.

End of transcript.
